alyssa: Heads-up — after last night's kernel-selector change we see a p99 spike for streaming chat on rtx-pool. p95 is fine but p99 jumped from ~210ms to ~480ms on 2048-token sessions. linked trace: https://perf.redwood/exp/4987 :eyes:

jordan: ugh. can you paste the top-level flame or perf-bot summary? wondering if kv-cache misses or kernel fallback is to blame.

alyssa: perf-bot summary pasted below. it attributes 65% of tail time to small-kernel warmup + handshake overhead when we pick the fast-4bit kernel. kv-cache miss rate increased ~12% for these sessions.

perf-bot: EXP 4987 — p95 214ms, p99 482ms, throughput (tokens/s) -2.1% vs baseline. Kernel selector toggled heuristics: prefer fast-4bit for attention widths < 1024. KV cache miss delta +12%.

vikram: important distinction: streaming chat has a handshake/first-token latency that's amortized differently than non-streaming completions. microbatch size interacts badly — with mb=4 we were batching 1-2 live tokens per batch and triggering kernel switches more often.

simon: did we measure the kernel switch cost alone? e.g. run identical sequence forcing kernel A->B and measure overhead?

alyssa: yes. cheap microbenchmark shows kernel switch + init ~120ms median, 300ms 95th when device busy. with mbsize=4 we saw switches every ~3rd request in the chat mix, with mbsize=2 switches every ~7th.

jordan: so larger mbsize reduces switches but increases queueing latency. we need SLO tradeoff numbers. what happens if we lower mbsize for streaming only, keep completions at higher mb?

alyssa: ran a small canary: streaming mb=2, completions mb=6. results: streaming p99 reduced to 230ms (good), p95 ~190ms. completions throughput dropped ~6% and p99 increased from 320ms to 380ms but still within target for that route. overall cost per token +1.8%.

vikram: that's promising. suggests route-level mbsize override is the right short-term fix. Longer-term we should make kernel-selector aware of streaming vs non-streaming semantics (avoid warm paths during handshake).

simon: also worth investigating kv-cache prefetching on handshake. If cache misses spike by 12% we pay both kv-rebuild + kernel cost. Can we keep a tiny per-client warm cache or prefetch last N tokens on socket reconnect?

alyssa: added a quick experiment: prefetch last_kv=64 for streaming sessions. preliminary shows kv misses down 7% and p99 improved another ~30ms. cost of prefetch negligible compared to p99 wins.

jordan: nice. combine per-route mb override + handshake-prefetch seems like a low-risk mitigation. action items?

alyssa: 1) roll routing override to canary (streaming: mb=2, completions: mb=6) — canary target user cohort 5%. 2) enable handshake-prefetch for streaming only. 3) add kernel-selector hint: avoid immediate kernel switch within X ms of session start (initially 500ms).

vikram: add profiling ticket to quantify kernel switch cost under load with different sequence lengths. include trace ids and experiment ids. 4) instrument kernel-switch events in flame traces so they show as explicit spans.

simon: I'll take 1+2 (canary + prefetch), jordan can own 3 and 4?

jordan: yep taking kernel-selector hint + instrumentation. will add config flag: "avoid_immediate_kernel_switch_ms": 500. we should make it per-route adjustable.

alyssa: sample config we used for canary: ```json
{"routes": {"chat-streaming": {"microbatch_size": 2, "handshake_prefetch_kv": 64, "kernel_hint": {"avoid_immediate_kernel_switch_ms": 500}}, "completions": {"microbatch_size": 6}}}
```

perf-bot: Canary EXP 4992 started. baseline: p99(streaming)=482ms. canary initial 1h: p99(streaming)=245ms, p95=200ms, throughput(streaming) -3.2%.

alyssa: decision from triage: roll canary to 25% for next 6h, monitor p99, p95, kv-miss-rate, and token throughput. if metrics stable, promote to 100% and then iterate on kernel-selector hint tuning.

vikram: longer-term items for backlog (separate tickets): - dynamic mbsize based on request token-length histogram - smarter kernel cost model that considers warmup + device load - persistent per-client kv-warm windows - microbench harness to emulate mixed chat/completions load

simon: one more data point: non-streaming completions benefit from higher mbsize for throughput. we should add a default route policy that picks mbsize by route-type not global.

jordan: creating rollout PR and canary dashboard: https://dash.redwood/canary/4992. will also add alert: if completions p99 rises >50ms vs baseline during canary, auto-rollback.

alyssa: thanks team. I'll post a short summary to #eng-releases when we hit 100% so product/ops know the perf/cost impacts. :thumbsup:

perf-bot: Note: label EXP-4992 in release notes and link traces EXP-4987 and EXP-4990 for root cause analysis.

jordan: assigning follow-ups in linear: LR-1128 (canary roll), LR-1129 (kernel hint), LR-1130 (kv-prefetch), LR-1131 (instrumentation).

alyssa: closing thread for now, will update after 25% canary run completes.
